# experiment-core

> Session lifecycle for operant experiments: drives a contingency-py reinforcement schedule through IDLE → RUNNING → REINFORCING → FINISHED, emits typed events (state changes, reinforcer start/end), applies exit conditions, and models experimental context and ABA/AAB/ABC renewal.

experiment-core is part of OperantKit, a set of Python/Rust packages for designing and running operant and respondent conditioning experiments (reinforcement schedules, session recording, analysis). Use it instead of hand-writing the session loop around a schedule: reinforcer delivery is an interval with its own start and end events, exit conditions (reinforcer count, time limit) are checked on every update, and every event can be forwarded to a sink for recording.

## Install

```bash
pip install experiment-core
```

## Minimal example

```python
from contingency_dsl import parse
from contingency import from_dsl
from experiment_core import ReinforcementCountExit, Session, SessionState

session = Session(from_dsl(parse("FR 3")), exit_condition=ReinforcementCountExit(count=2))
session.start(0.0)
responses = 0
for t in range(1, 11):  # one response per second
    if session.state is SessionState.REINFORCING:
        session.end_reinforcement(float(t))  # 1-s reinforcer access ends
        continue
    responses += 1
    session.update(float(t), responses)
print(session.state.name, session.reinforcement_count)  # FINISHED 2
```

`Session.update(timestamp, total_responses)` advances a single-operandum session; `Session.handle_response_on(index, timestamp)` records a response on one operandum of a concurrent schedule. For a callback-style driver with event sinks use session-runner.

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/OperantKit/experiment-core/blob/main/README.md): role, 30-second example, why not to hand-roll a session loop, module map
- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OperantKit/experiment-core/blob/main/AGENTS.md): when to use this package and what not to do

## Related packages

- [contingency-py](https://github.com/OperantKit/contingency-py): the schedule engine a `Session` drives (`pip install contingency-py`)
- [contingency-dsl-py](https://github.com/OperantKit/contingency-dsl-py): parser for schedule expressions such as `Conc(VI30s, VI60s, COD=2s)`
- [session-runner](https://github.com/OperantKit/session-runner): callback-style driver that forwards session events to sinks (`pip install session-runner`)
- [session-recorder](https://github.com/OperantKit/session-recorder): writes session events to OKL v1 files (`pip install session-recorder`)
- [experiment-io](https://github.com/OperantKit/experiment-io): hardware abstraction (virtual and serial operanda) and the hardware-driven loop
